title: Lattices of rings grow by bands, not by single rings
subject: Networks of rings joined by shared contacts, read with the canonical knot test on their space-time law
conclusion: Every n x m torus of equally spaced rule-60 rings with n, m at least 3 has a half-turn at every contact, so growth by whole bands round the torus or by splitting every ring into blocks keeps every contact persistent at every stage. A single new ring breaks it with one contact, with two not side by side, or as a bubble on a corner from p to q whenever some contact is reached from q and reaches p.
